title: introduce-quant-fallback-family-and-batchshape-rewriter
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Adds an automated quantization fallback family and a batch-shape rewriter that synthesizes safe microbatch fallbacks for constrained GPU configurations; no visible API changes for end users. Recommended rollout with canary on low-memory SKU tenants.
description: Context: Some tenant workloads hit OOM/latency cliffs when a single quant profile or batch template is applied across diverse hardware. This PR introduces two companion pieces: 1) a quant-fallback-family abstraction that encodes an ordered set of compatible quant profiles (e.g., int8->q4_a->q8_dynamic) with quality-preservation thresholds and automated fallbacks when kernel failures or validity checks occur; 2) a batch-shape-rewriter that rewrites tenant batch templates at runtime to insert microbatch fallbacks and conservative pad/truncation rules for GPUs with lower max-seqlen or reduced tensor memory. Motivation: reduce incident-driven hotfixes and automate safe downgrades so we avoid broad rollbacks while preserving unit economics. Scope: runtime components, a small policy registry, unit tests, e2e smoke test, and a lightweight telemetry tag for fallback events. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-5012) - [x] unit tests for rewriter and fallback switch - [x] integration smoke that exercises int8->q4 fallback path - [x] telemetry emitted for fallback events and batch-rewrite events - [x] docs stub for ops and rollout recommendations Implementation notes: commits below summarize the changes; the runtime adds a new interface QuantFallbackFamily with a catalog entry for common families and an evaluation hook invoked during model init and on kernel failure; the batch-shape-rewriter plugs into the batching pipeline pre-placement and can produce 1) adjusted batch shapes that prefer narrower cumulative token budgets per device and 2) microbatch split plans that preserve latency SLOs for tail requests. Safety: conservative defaults are enforced; the rewriter is disabled by default for existing tenants and enabled in canary mode via tenant flags. Rollout plan: canary on dedicated-lowmem pool for 48h, monitor redwood.fallback.rate and latency 95/99; if stable, flip tenant-defaults after 7 days. Links: design doc: https://linear.app/org/ENG-5012; incident context SUP-3221; related policy discussion ENG-5080.

review_comments: Marco Diaz: Overall design looks sound but please add a unit test for a chained kernel failure where int8 kernel fails fast and q4 also reports degraded-likelihood; ensure we record the exact failure reason for later correlation.
Aisha Kapoor: Added chained-failure unit test and expanded telemetry to include failure_reason; also added a guard to avoid retry storms by adding a 10s cooldown per model instance.
Emily Chen: Could the rewriter ever create a batch shape that violates our placement allocator assumptions? Please ensure the allocator rejects unsafe shapes and emits a clear metric.

Aisha Kapoor: The rewriter validates generated shapes against allocator constraints; unsafe shapes are dropped and the original template is returned with a telemetry tag. Added tests for allocator rejection path.
Sven Johansson: CI showed a flaky e2e assertion on embedded latency; I think we need a tighter sleep in the smoke test or a retry wrapper.
Aisha Kapoor: Reworked the smoke test to use a retry loop with backoff and added a comment explaining the nondeterminism on shared CI runners.
Emily Chen: Approving pending green CI and a short changelog entry for ops. Marco please take a final pass on the telemetry fields.
Marco Diaz: Approved. All telemetry fields look good and include failure_reason, fallback_index, and previous_shape_hash.
ci_summary: CI pipeline: lint -> unit-tests -> integration-smoke -> e2e. First run: lint pass, unit-tests pass, integration-smoke failed intermittently (timing), rerun succeeded; e2e smoke run passed on rerun. Coverage delta: +1.2% in runtime/batching.
notes_for_ops: Default off for existing tenants. To enable for a tenant: set tenant.flags.enable_quant_fallback=true and tenant.flags.enable_batch_rewriter=canary. Monitor metrics: redwood.fallback.rate, redwood.batch_rewrite.count, redwood.model.oom.count. If fallback.rate>0.5% persistently, open ENG-ops ticket and revert the tenant flag.
